59237701.s: Al Soudah is a mountain tourist destination in the Asir region, about 20 kilometres from the city of Abha. It lies at an altitude of nearly 3,000 metres above sea level, and its mountains are covered with dense juniper trees that form stunning natural forests.
59237701.b:
Al Soudah is a mountain tourist destination in the Asir region, about 20 kilometres from the city of Abha. It lies at an altitude of nearly 3,000 metres above sea level, and its mountains are covered with dense juniper trees that form stunning natural forests.

Al Soudah overlooks the Tihama region, so magnifying viewers have been installed in some parts as viewpoints for watching the lowlands, valleys and neighbouring villages on the Tihama plains. It is known for its mild climate in summer and cold climate in winter compared with the surrounding areas. It includes Al Soudah Tourist Village with its varied services, and is linked to Rijal Alma village in Tihama by cable car.

Near Al Soudah lie the villages of Bahat Rabi'ah, which include Al Muhtatabah Park, known for its natural waterfalls and the lakes formed by flowing water and rainfall, and King Abdulaziz Park lies north of Al Soudah, with its natural scenery and varied services for visitors.

59237698.s: Al Soudah village is part of the city of Abha in the Asir region. It includes several parks, most notably Asir Tourist Park and King Abdulaziz Al Saud Park, and some hotels that offer wonderful mountain views. The village also has various facilities providing the different services visitors need, which are overseen by the Asir Region Municipality.

59237693.s: The High City is known for its beautiful views over Tihama to the south-east and over the city of Abha to the north-west. The city covers an area of about 26,000 square metres and has many resorts, hotels and residential villas that meet visitors' needs, as well as many varied, upscale cafes and restaurants.

59237692.s: A quiet park at the top of a hill with a children's playground, benches and wide views over the city. The park overlooks the city of Abha from above with a panoramic view and has vast green spaces and a variety of trees. The best time to visit is winter, to see the fog drifting through the park. The park offers many benches for resting and enjoying the surroundings, and has a number of green terraces.

Abu Khayal Park got its name because in winter fog spreads thickly through the park, so that those in it see it as if it were shadowy figures in a landscape.

59237621.s: Al Dabab Walkway (Fog Walkway) is one of the most beautiful tourist destinations in Abha, giving visitors the feeling of walking among the clouds. It is in the Al Dabab district on the mountain tops, overlooking Aqabat Dhala' and the Tihama plains, and its suspended walkway extends for nearly seven kilometres and is up to 14 metres wide.

It is in the Al Dabab district on the mountain tops, overlooking Aqabat Dhala' and the Tihama plains, and its suspended walkway extends for nearly seven kilometres and is up to 14 metres wide.

The walkway has shaded seating, green spaces, children's play areas and artificial waterfalls that give the place an enchanting atmosphere in the evening, as well as restaurants, restrooms, prayer rooms and car parks.

59237597.s: Abha Dam Lake Parks are located west of the city on the banks of the lake formed by Abha Dam, with wide green spaces suited to outings and family gatherings in the midst of nature.
59237597.b:
Abha Dam Lake Parks are located west of the city on the banks of the lake formed by Abha Dam, with wide green spaces suited to outings and family gatherings in the midst of nature.

Abha Dam was rebuilt in the reign of King Faisal and opened in 1394 AH / 1974 CE to hold flood waters coming down from the mountains. It is about 350 metres long and 30 metres high, and its lake holds more than two million cubic metres of water, making it one of the most prominent natural landmarks of Abha.

The park is also concerned with conveying meaningful messages through the arts, such as the importance of protecting the environment and recycling. It has play areas, and since it opened it has been a major attraction for visitors.

59237558.s: Al Muftaha Village is one of the tourist villages in the city of Abha in the south of Saudi Arabia. The village is built in an architectural style drawn from the heritage and civilisation of the Asir region. It is a group of adjoining buildings along inner and outer passageways, built using the traditional building methods of Abha, with small openings, thick walls and the use of "raqaf" (stone slabs) to protect the mud walls from rain and provide shade on the building's facade.

59237504.s: Art Street lies in the heart of Abha in the Asir region of south-western Saudi Arabia and extends about 200 metres. It is considered one of the most important tourist sites in the region and a meeting point for art lovers, both artists and enthusiasts, from all over Saudi Arabia. The street has 10 galleries, a theatre for holding concerts, and many local and international restaurants and cafes. As far as the eye can see the street is decorated with varied artworks by local artists, and colourful umbrellas are spread out like a dazzling carnival between two rows of jacaranda trees.

59237500.s: Al Habala village lies in the Asir region about 57 kilometres from the city of Abha. It is a hanging village whose stone houses were built on the edge of a towering rocky cliff in the Sarawat mountains, and it was named Al Habala (from "hibal", ropes) because ropes were once the only way to reach it and to carry supplies to its residents.
59237500.b:
Al Habala village lies in the Asir region about 57 kilometres from the city of Abha. It is a hanging village whose stone houses were built on the edge of a towering rocky cliff in the Sarawat mountains, and it was named Al Habala (from "hibal", ropes) because ropes were once the only way to reach it and to carry supplies to its residents.

As soon as King Faisal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud learned of the hardship of the people of Al Habala, he ordered a modern village to be built for them, known as King Faisal Charity Village, which was built on level ground and to which all the people of Al Habala moved. The old place became a tourist site, as the tourism company succeeded in turning it into a tourist resort by building a number of tourism projects, such as modern residential units equipped with services and entertainment facilities like swimming and other games. At the top of the viewpoint overlooking the old village a restaurant serving a variety of meals to visitors was built, and cable cars (a "telepherique") were also installed. Modern means of transport have also encouraged some residents to look after their old farms, which are now set aside for receiving visitors and serving drinks and food.
59237500.a: Al Habala, Ahad Rafidah, Asir Province

59233263.s: Ekmah is a mountainous area from which a narrow valley descends, dark in colour with a reddish tint and very tall. It has many Lihyanite inscriptions on its rock faces, which document the history of the Kingdom of Lihyan, its civilisation, its social interactions, its foreign relations and its internal organisation and laws. It is close to the site of Al Khuraybah, where the Lihyan state lived.

59231766.s: The Lion Tombs are rectangular recesses carved into the rock, varying in colour between red and white, each side measuring 80 cm and two metres deep. They are called the Lion Tombs because of the lion carved above the facades of the tombs. Researchers note that the lion was chosen for these facades because of what it represents in the cultures of the ancient world as a symbol of strength and might. The tombs date back to the fifth century BCE, the early period of the Kingdom of Dadan, which ruled the region at that time.

59231645.s: Madain Saleh was known in ancient times as the city of Hegra. It is an archaeological site in the Hejaz region of the Arabian Peninsula, in north-west Saudi Arabia, specifically in AlUla Governorate in the Madinah region. The site occupies a strategic location on the road linking the south of the Arabian Peninsula with Mesopotamia, the Levant and Egypt, and its historical fame comes from its position on the ancient trade route that linked southern Arabia and the Levant.
59231645.b:
Madain Saleh was known in ancient times as the city of Hegra. It is an archaeological site in the Hejaz region of the Arabian Peninsula, in north-west Saudi Arabia, specifically in AlUla Governorate in the Madinah region. The site occupies a strategic location on the road linking the south of the Arabian Peninsula with Mesopotamia, the Levant and Egypt, and its historical fame comes from its position on the ancient trade route that linked southern Arabia and the Levant.

Hegra is the name of the homeland of Thamud in Wadi Al Qura between Madinah and Tabuk. Hegra is mentioned in the Quran as the home of the people of Thamud, who responded to the call of the Prophet of Allah Saleh, then turned away from their religion and hamstrung the she-camel that Allah had sent them as a sign, and so were destroyed by the Cry.

Madain Saleh is one of the most important Nabataean cities after their capital Petra. It contains the largest southern settlement of the Nabataean kingdom after Petra in Jordan, which is 500 km away. Its most notable cultural role dates to the first century BCE and the first century CE, during the flourishing of the Nabataean state and before its fall to the Roman Empire in 106 CE. Hegra is believed to have continued its civilisation until the fourth century CE, and it was the capital of the Kingdom of Lihyan in the north of the Arabian Peninsula.

The remains of Madain Saleh include 153 carved rock facades, as well as a number of Islamic remains consisting of a number of forts and the remains of the Hejaz Railway line, which extends for 13 km, along with the station and locomotives. In 2008 the site was inscribed on the World Heritage List, becoming the first site in Saudi Arabia to be inscribed.

59231603.s: The Old Town is a completely abandoned town in AlUla Governorate in the west of Saudi Arabia. It is called Al Dirah and has old heritage buildings, mosques and markets dating back about 7 centuries, and it is 22 kilometres from Madain Saleh.
59231603.b:
The Old Town is a completely abandoned town in AlUla Governorate in the west of Saudi Arabia. It is called Al Dirah and has old heritage buildings, mosques and markets dating back about 7 centuries, and it is 22 kilometres from Madain Saleh.

The heritage town appears almost as a single building because its housing units, estimated at 870, are so close together, with narrow, winding alleys running between them. It is divided into two parts: Harat Al Shuqayq in the north and Harat Al Hafa in the south.

59231533.s: The Ghramil Mountains (Magnificent Rocks of Buraikah) are marvellous red rock formations that have taken different shapes and sizes through natural erosion over thousands of years, forming a unique, iconic picture with a charming and beautiful desert view. They are among the most prominent natural landmarks reflecting the geological diversity of the AlUla region.
